# Internal project entry: independent expected results

## Status and source of truth

These expectations precede the runtime output template and any new candidate.
Only three small synthetic scenarios are proposed here. Their raw inputs are to be
prepared separately before execution; no tests or business operations were run by
writing this file. Do not derive the oracle from a renderer, validator, previously
generated PROJECT, or screenshot.

The tentative skill name is `organize-project`. This file does not select that
name, a fixed section order, a table layout, a diagram technology or a new schema.
It specifies observable requirements, not the model's internal thinking process.
Scenario-specific paper/Run/Attempt counts and toy values are not universal rules.

## Common visible result

### Internal entry and public documentation

- The managed research project's PROJECT is an internal, independently readable
  entry. Its README remains the public-facing document and remains unchanged
  unless a separate, explicit edit is in scope.
- Internal does not mean automatically excluded from internal Git. Do not modify
  ignore rules, delete README, publish either document, commit, push or change a
  release manifest just to establish this distinction.
- A preview-only request produces a clearly labelled candidate or conversation
  preview, not a silent overwrite of an existing PROJECT.

### Goals, present state and evidence

- The project's goal and present state are understandable without following every
  link. The entry identifies when its observations were checked and where the
  supporting declarations/records came from.
- Distinguish source declarations, statically inspected code/files, recorded
  execution outcomes, missing information and checks not performed. A date in a
  fixture is not a current verification date. If no check was made, say so rather
  than inventing a verified timestamp.
- Successful record status does not prove actual execution, reproduction,
  scientific superiority, reader behavior or externally verified backup.

### Direct code and configuration navigation

- Every selected code/configuration entry has a direct, resolvable file link or an
  explicit missing/unavailable state. A homepage or chain of intermediate pages is
  not a substitute for the requested entry.
- The module relationship figure matches the actual bounded evidence. A literal
  call or import can support a static code relationship; it does not prove runtime
  data movement or execution success. A merely claimed or uninspected relation
  must not be drawn as established causality/call flow.
- Preserve uncertainty without inventing modules, edges, code paths or behavior
  simply to complete a diagram. The chosen graphical carrier remains editable
  where applicable and readable; no new Hub is required.

### Experiment and result navigation

- Every selected Run, Attempt and Artifact is individually discoverable with its
  existing identity, declared status and direct record/result entry. Failed and
  retry/replay records remain visible when selected; they do not disappear behind
  a latest-success summary.
- Preserve Run versus Attempt. Retrying or replaying the same Run is not another
  independent experiment or statistical replicate.
- Preserve missing artifacts and incomplete/remote-only evidence. Do not invent
  a local plot or verified result; do not execute code to fill an empty entry.
- Backup pending or unverified remains visible. A recovery copy, local presence
  or a content hash alone must not be described as verified backup.

### Paper units and related materials

- The selected paper's source/material note, analysis Markdown and editable
  Canvas each have a distinct, direct entry when available. The owning unit is
  reused rather than copying its analysis or creating a new canonical paper.
- Use the explicit qualified reference and selected source/reader mapping where
  supplied. Matching titles or filenames do not establish identity or ownership.
- A missing analysis/Canvas and an unqueried reader stay visible as such. An
  unqueried link is not reader-tested; do not fabricate a cross-Source wikilink or
  make a fake successful opening claim.

### One authoritative detailed plan

- With an inline plan, PROJECT contains the authoritative detail and does not
  create an unnecessary second SCHEDULE containing another editable copy.
- With an explicit external SCHEDULE, PROJECT summarizes the current plan and
  links to its authoritative detail. It must not repeat a second independently
  maintained detailed plan.
- Missing dates remain undated. Conflicting detailed plans without a declared
  authority remain an unresolved decision; do not silently choose, merge, delete
  or assign dates to make them appear consistent.

### Preservation and scope

- Preserve existing human-authored material, existing paper bodies/Canvas, README,
  source/configuration files, experimental records and identities. Updates require
  an explicitly permitted file boundary and current-byte protection; a preview
  gives no overwrite permission.
- No Hub/service requirement, registration/init-project step, experiment run,
  migration, paper-body duplication, new ownership ledger, external synchronization
  or Git/release operation is introduced by organizing the entry.
- All visible language, labels, source states and completion claims are consistent.
  Machine IDs and hashes can support references but cannot replace readable text.
  Missing items and unperformed checks cannot be hidden by polished presentation.

## Three minimum scenarios to prepare

### `complete-inline` — supported navigation, inline plan

Hand-write a tiny project goal/status declaration, a public README with a distinct
human paragraph, two code files with one inspectable relationship, one config,
selected experiment records, and explicit references to a paper note, analysis and
Canvas. The detailed plan is inline and not separately authored in SCHEDULE.
Records and values are explicitly synthetic, not executions.

Expected: an internal PROJECT candidate with direct entries, the bounded static
relationship and its evidence state, the complete selected experiment hierarchy,
all three paper-unit entrances, and one detailed inline plan. The public README,
paper files and experiment inputs remain byte-identical. No external application
is opened to claim reader success and no experiment is executed.

### `sparse-external-plan` — incomplete evidence, external authority

Hand-write an independent SCHEDULE as the declared detailed plan authority. Include
a missing selected file/artifact, an uninspected relationship claimed only in a
note, a successful retry of the same Run, a missing paper analysis or Canvas, an
unqueried reader, an undated milestone and backup pending/unverified.

Expected: PROJECT exposes each limitation beside the corresponding item; its plan
is only a summary/link to SCHEDULE. The uncertain code relationship is not asserted
as verified flow, the successful retry is not counted as another experiment, and
no date, file, reader success or backup verification is invented. No missing item
is silently omitted or generated by executing business operations.

### `preservation-conflict` — preview-only human-content protection

Hand-write existing PROJECT and README human paragraphs and conflicting detailed
plan statements in PROJECT/SCHEDULE. Supply no decision about plan authority and
request only a preview. Existing paper units remain outside the output boundary.

Expected: an explicitly labelled independent candidate or conversation preview,
an understandable conflict/decision request, and zero changes to all original
files. Do not rewrite human content, select one plan, copy papers, create a new
owner, alter ignore rules or publish the internal entry.

## Independent evaluation and visible handoff

Compare original raw files and their byte baselines with the delivered entry and
this handwritten inventory. Evaluate link targets from the selected input roots,
not from a product-generated success flag. Do not execute project source files,
recipes or experiments; no network or application launch is needed for this slice.

Deliver the actual candidate, a concise list of inspected/uninspected inputs and
an independent result report with failures and preserved bytes. Say exactly where
to open it in VS Code, which direct links to try, and what goal/navigation/diagram/
plan clarity the user should judge. Native link opening and visual usability remain
pending until separately observed or explicitly accepted by the human; automatic
content checks and installed-skill triggering are separate results.
